author: D. N. Kessler
title: John Kennedy comments on Memorial Day tributes and U.S.-UK defense issues
text:
John Kennedy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana, addressed a range of topics on his social media accounts between May 25 and May 27, 2026. His posts included reflections on Memorial Day, concerns about U.S. military assets in the Indo-Pacific region, and a personal message.
On May 25, Kennedy posted a tribute to fallen service members: “On Memorial Day, we honor the brave men and women who gave their lives so the rest of us could live free. America is the greatest country in human history because of the heroes who love her more than themselves. Becky and I are praying for their families today.”
The following day, Kennedy expressed apprehension over potential changes in control of Diego Garcia: “There is no military asset as important as Diego Garcia when it comes to America’s ability to deter China. It would be weapons-grade stupid to sit by as the U.K. signs it away to a nation in Xi Jinping’s pocket. Read my latest in @NewsweekOpinion:” The tweet references an opinion piece published in Newsweek Opinion regarding strategic security concerns.
On May 27, Kennedy shared a brief message: “Margaret has something she wants to share.”
Senator John Kennedy holds advanced degrees from Vanderbilt University, the University of Virginia School of Law, and Oxford University ( official website ). He serves on Senate committees related to appropriations, banking, budget, and judiciary matters. Additionally, he holds top Republican positions on subcommittees for energy and water development as well as economic policy. Beyond legislative duties, Kennedy contributes to education as an adjunct professor and substitute teacher and has authored works on constitutional law and product liability. During his academic career he was executive editor of the Virginia Law Review and president of his senior class at Vanderbilt University.
